prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production 2D Engineer survivor animation for Grave Accord. Image 1 is the approved four-view Engineer identity reference; Image 2 contains the exact shipped seed for this facing and is an identity/facing reference, not a scene to reproduce. Keep the same adult woman, auburn hair in one bun, brass goggles resting above the forehead, teal knee-length split work coat with rolled sleeves, rust neck scarf, brown crossed leather straps/tool belt/pouches, compact rectangular brown backpack, dark trousers, gloves and boots. She carries ONE compact brass cylindrical firearm in her physical RIGHT hand, and no shield. Keep her face and practical costume recognizable, with the same body proportions, camera and palette. Use restrained dry black ink and matte opaque gouache, broad quiet teal cloth planes and a few clean selective contours. Avoid glossy gradients, excessive scratches, decorative filigree, dense tiny mechanisms, or noise. Maintain two arms/two legs, connected hands and rigid equipment, no mirrored asymmetric arms, no duplicate gun or detached accessories.
Every pose faces NORTH, facing AWAY from the viewer as in the lower-left figure of Image 1. Show the back of her auburn bun, teal coat, crossed straps and brown rectangular backpack. No face on the back of the head. Her firearm stays in her physical RIGHT hand at viewer RIGHT; left hand is unarmed at viewer LEFT.
Draw exactly 6 complete full-body poses as one coherent downed animation sheet, arranged in THREE columns and TWO rows, reading top-left to top-right then bottom-left to bottom-right, on an approximately 1536 by 1024 transparent canvas. Fill exactly these 6 cells with no extra figure. Action: One continuous non-graphic incapacitation: 1 full upright ready guard as scale reference; 2 knees buckle and torso sinks; 3 one knee reaches the ground; 4 lower onto her physical right hip/side; 5 settle into a low side-supported posture; 6 fully incapacitated but alive, lying low on her side with connected natural limbs, the gun still lowered alongside her RIGHT hand/arm and the backpack attached behind the torso. Left hand is free and may support the fall. The final two poses must clearly show incapacitation, not standing. Keep the same facing/camera and practical costume. The lying figure becomes naturally shorter and wider; never enlarge crouched or lying poses to fill their cells. No blood, injuries or dramatic effects.
Use the full upright neutral pose as the common size reference; all frames share one character scale. Keep roomy clear gutters and padding around EVERY full silhouette and a consistent ground baseline within each row. BACKGROUND: genuine RGBA transparency, alpha zero everywhere outside the figures, including between legs and around props. No floor, ground shadow, scenery, haze, glow, vignette, colored backdrop, checker pattern, text, labels, numbers or grid lines. Preserve clean ink edges and matte gouache inside the silhouettes. Deliver the entire coherent sheet, never separately posed illustrations.
